questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing my exchange destination I took several things into account. First of all I wanted to go somewhere I hadn't visited, followed by a University with courses taught in English, but most importantly a destination where I could go into the mountains and/or nature and hike!! A combination of all these lead me to choose Edinburgh, Scotland. Which in my opinion is a perfect destination for exchange as it combines cute city with good nightlife, a good university and in beautiful surroundings!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I highly recommend to study abroad (even though admin stuff sucks). I especially recommend Edinburgh for nature- and pint-loving people!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. The University of Edinburgh platforms for students are easy to comprehend and they send many different informative emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Upon arrival I received a personal tutor, whom I could ask for help throughout my entire exchange. My tutor reached out to me already before semester start, which was nice, as I had problems with my courses. He assisted me (in-person) with solving the problems and was always quick by email as well. As I was in the School of Biological Science, I am not sure if the other schools had the same system with tutors. 
But there was a lot of informative meetings in the beginning of the semester as well!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: On or off campus, no matter what it is a nightmare finding affordable housing for students in Edinburgh. There is a huge housing crisis going on and prices are even higher than in Copenhagen. I found housing two days before arrival after calling the accommodation service at Edinburgh Uni multiple times until they found a very expensive room at one of the student accommodations. My suggestion is to start early, use the available facebook pages for housing in Edinburgh and if you want housing through uni, either apply months before or call them every day. Many people did not find a place to stay until after semester start.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city is very small, so there is really no such thing as off-campus. It is very easy to get around.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Deep breaths :)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration for courses starts when applying for Edinburgh. It can be a bit difficult to figure out which courses one can apply for and not, but there is a lot of available webpages through Uni website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Many different web tools including course descriptions and course timetable browser

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Well, it is common that they change the timetable up until semester start, so all my three courses were overlapping! This was of course a shame, but my tutor helped me finding new courses that did not overlap (also by using the course timetable browser, available through Uni Edinburgh).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Remember to double check that your courses are not overlapping by using the Course Timetable Browser
https://browser.ted.is.ed.ac.uk/
Ask your school for help or your personal tutor
You also have two weeks after semester starts, where you still have time to change courses if your unhappy
Remember to apply for many courses when doing your pre-approval application at uCPH

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two level 9 courses (Year 3) and one level 11 course (Year 4). The level was a bit lower than what I am used to at CPH, otherwise great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: No group work. All assignments were individual. Lectures were shorter and fewer. Lab work was not as independent compared to CPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Molecular & Synthetic Plant Biology 3
Molecular Microbiology 3
Bioinformatics 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Molecular & Synthetic Plant Biology 3!! Small course, enthusiastic professors and students, a lot of help, fun lab work. Great if you like plants! This was no doubt my favorite course.

questions.answer: My bike needed repair a few times :) I also went to the highlands quite a lot, so a lot of transportation.

questions.answer:
Rent was more expensive (but it was catered so food was included).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many. So many different clubs, socials, activities, societies. I was a part of the Uni Hillwalking Club, Fitness, Kickboxing and Feminist Society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the hillwalking club. If you like bouldering as well, join the mountaineering club and the bouldering in the Pleasance fitness center. I would also recommend the Fungi Society. There is a lot of societies for bands as well (music).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The highlands! Explore all the great Munroes (mountains) of Scotland, go to Ceilidh (folk dance), dance in general, drink pints, explore Edinburgh, go to Glasgow or Manchester. Visit all the cute small book shops. Go to Arthurs Seat, Dean Village, Stockbridge, the Pentlands, Morningside.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The scots are very welcoming and kind! And funny.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring good footwear (walking boots)
Join a society / club
Use the University libraries (especially Law and Nucleus library)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Admin sucks, but you'll survive

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Walking in the mountains and forests with friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning when you miss your friends! And of course exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go go go

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
